declarations.coverage: Drafted from the repository tree by `discovery/draft-documentation-scope.mjs`: every file Git keeps under the documentation roots `docs` and `factory/docs`, a new index for each of their directories without one, the development guide, and the domain glossaries and context maps the rules identify. Paths other declarations own are left out, including `docs/agents/project.md`, which the `project-agent-guidance` declaration now owns, and so is each README.md outside the documentation roots. The retired Repository Standards skills are left out because this run removes them. Open questions decided as in the previously confirmed scope: `factory/docs` is a documentation root, as the repository conformance test's scope and the factory package's own documentation tree establish, and every directory under it already has an index; `authoring-notes.md` stays in place at the root and is covered; `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` is license notices, `discovery`, `guidance` and `rules` hold authored standards source inputs referenced by standards.yaml, and `vendor` holds preserved upstream snapshots, so all of those are excluded. No moves, new indexes or link repairs are needed.

declarations.coverage: Intentionally empty local scope: the authored remote setup fixes configure GitHub settings on lutzseverino/repo-canon, the only repository the Git remotes name, and the reviewer check reads the repository-owned .github/pull-request-reviewer.json without writing it. Observed with authenticated gh: the repository is PUBLIC, and the repository-level REPO_CANON_RUNS_ON variable is absent, so the setting is unset and the installed jobs use the hosted ubuntu-latest default. The owner, lutzseverino, is a user account rather than an organization, so no organization-level value can be inherited. The maintainer requested this update; discovery and assessment set no variable.

Reviewed the root and factory package manifests, the development guides, the glossary map and vendor README provenance. The factory directory is Scriptorium, a separately released package with its own package.json, scripts, tests, glossary and documentation tree, so it is a Project with its existing factory/README.md. The root package owns all other maintenance and validation; operations, discovery, guidance, rules and scripts have no independent Project commands; test fixtures, vendored snapshots and documentation are excluded. No missing Project README is needed.
